entities.name: Étienne-Denis Pasquier
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Étienne Denis Pasquier (1767–1862) was a French statesman and jurist who was one of the most remarkable political survivors of the Napoleonic and post-Napoleonic era. Serving successive regimes — Empire, Bourbon Restoration, and the July Monarchy — he held major offices under each, including Minister of Justice, Minister of Foreign Affairs, President of the Chamber of Peers, and Chancellor of France. His exceptional longevity (he died at 94) and his willingness to serve each successive regime without conspicuous ideological commitment made him both invaluable and somewhat cynically criticized as the quintessential political opportunist.

His memoirs are a primary historical source for the Napoleonic and Restoration periods — the observations of a man who knew everyone and served everyone.

Napoleon reportedly said: 'Pasquier can serve anyone — he serves France.'

He was Chancellor of France and the longest-serving major statesman of his era.
